features.limitations: The exact-engine native SQLite fixture uses a synthetic validation callback, not Core Data. The separate native Core Data fixture compiles the complete production PersistentContainer and original models; it exercises v17.6-to-v17.7 DELETE and committed-WAL migration with generic managed-object classes, not account/keychain code. Both require macOS and matching Xcode/Swift/C toolchains and derive the Swift language mode from the actual SideStore Release target; use distinct fresh output directories outside the source tree via RECOVERY_ENGINE_OUTPUT and RECOVERY_COREDATA_OUTPUT. Set SIDESTORE_ROOT to the matching acquired owner checkout for the real-source case/input inventory gate in the builder receipt tests. That gate and portable runner/source tests never substitute for native execution. Source reservations do not exclude independent legacy filesystem-only Apps writers; pre/post inventories reject observed edits. No arbitrary divergent-store merge, power-loss durability, physical-device upgrade or app-group entitlement success is claimed. Repeated native command references describe shared inputs; one complete invocation covers them. Cache qualification uses the exact production Apps getter with an inert optional-URL MaintenanceManager boundary, not the recovery engine. Native setup verification requires matching BUILDER_ROOT, SOURCES_ROOT, SWIFTC, a fresh SETUP_RECOVERY_OUTPUT outside source checkouts and the reviewed same-graph SETUP_RECOVERY_CONTRACT; source generation and portable controls do not prove compilation or execution. Startup guard and model-resource controls have two distinct commands: --source-only runs 14 portable cases and explicitly reports NATIVE_NOT_RUN; the mandatory-Swift command runs 16 cases including two extracted-production Swift fixtures. These fixtures do not execute real application startup, Core Data or a physical device. The portable preflight cannot replace the mandatory same-run native startup receipt.
